en.description: Wispr Flow, Typeless, Superwhisper, VoiceInk, MacWhisper, Aqua Voice, Apple Dictation and more: price, local or cloud, and who each Mac dictation app suits.
heading: The Mac dictation apps worth knowing,
side by side.
en.intro: There are now more than a dozen ways to talk instead of type on a Mac. They split on two questions: where your voice is transcribed, and what you pay. This page puts them in one table, then says who each one suits.

Many local models, including SenseVoice; AI cleanup that can run locally
Local models with an optional hosted tier
Free local dictation into any app, mixed Chinese and English
Fast cloud dictation with voice commands
Cloud dictation across Mac, Windows and iPhone
Short dictation with nothing to install

sections.heading: Cloud or local is the first choice
body: [Wispr Flow](wispr-flow-alternative), [Typeless](typeless-alternative), [Aqua Voice](aqua-voice-alternative) and [Willow Voice](willow-voice-alternative) send your audio to their servers. That buys them large models and AI rewriting, and it is why they meter words and charge monthly. They also stop working when the connection does.

TypeAloud, [VoiceInk](voiceink-alternative), [MacWhisper](macwhisper-alternative) and the free tiers of [Superwhisper](superwhisper-alternative) and [Spokenly](spokenly-alternative) run a speech model on your Mac. Nothing is uploaded, there is no quota, and they work offline. The trade-off is a one-time model download and wanting an Apple Silicon Mac.

sections.heading: Then: an input method, or a transcription tool?
body: Some apps behave like a keyboard: hold a key, speak, and the text appears where you were typing. Wispr Flow, Typeless, Superwhisper, VoiceInk, Spokenly and TypeAloud work this way.
MacWhisper is built around recordings. It is excellent at turning an interview or a meeting into a transcript, and it has a Dictation feature too, but files are the centre of the app.

sections.heading: Prices and head-to-heads
body: For the subscription details, see [Wispr Flow pricing](wispr-flow-pricing) and [Typeless pricing](typeless-pricing). If you are choosing between two of them, there are direct comparisons of [Wispr Flow and Typeless](wispr-flow-vs-typeless), [Wispr Flow and Superwhisper](wispr-flow-vs-superwhisper), and [Superwhisper and MacWhisper](superwhisper-vs-macwhisper).

sections.heading: By use case
body: Looking for something specific: [free dictation with no word limit](free-dictation-mac), [open-source dictation](open-source-dictation-mac), [voice input for Claude Code and Cursor](voice-coding), [an answer to Whisper's trouble with mixed Chinese and English](whisper-chinese-english), [private dictation that never uploads audio](private-dictation), or help [writing long documents by voice](dictate-long-form). New to this? Start with [how to voice type on a Mac](how-to-voice-type-mac).

sections.heading: How to choose
body: Start with where the audio goes: if it must stay on your Mac, only the local apps qualify. Then the language: for Chinese, or Chinese mixed with English, prefer a Chinese-trained model. Then price and extras: AI rewriting, phone apps and team features are where the paid cloud apps earn their price. Try two candidates with sentences you actually say before paying for a year.

faq.q: What is the best free dictation app for Mac?
faq.a: It depends on your language and privacy needs. Free local options include Superwhisper's free tier, Spokenly, Handy and TypeAloud; macOS Dictation is built in but listens in one language at a time and keeps no history.

faq.q: Which Mac dictation apps work offline?
faq.a: The local ones: VoiceInk, MacWhisper, TypeAloud, and Superwhisper or Spokenly with a local model. Cloud apps such as Wispr Flow, Typeless, Aqua Voice and Willow Voice need a connection.

faq.q: Which one is best for Chinese?
faq.a: Look at the model. Qwen3-ASR and SenseVoice were trained with a lot of Chinese and detect the language as they go, which matters when you mix in English; Whisper settles on one language per recording ([details](whisper-chinese-english)). Test two candidates with your own sentences.

faq.q: Which dictation apps work on Intel Macs?
faq.a: Cloud apps work on any supported Mac. Local apps vary: some require Apple Silicon, others run on Intel more slowly. Check each app's requirements.

sections.heading: 先选云端还是本地
body: [Wispr Flow](wispr-flow-alternative)、[Typeless](typeless-alternative)、[Aqua Voice](aqua-voice-alternative) 和 [Willow Voice](willow-voice-alternative) 都把音频传到自己的服务器。这让它们能用大模型、做 AI 改写，也正因如此它们要按字数计量、按月收费，断网就用不了。

TypeAloud、[VoiceInk](voiceink-alternative)、[MacWhisper](macwhisper-alternative)，以及 [Superwhisper](superwhisper-alternative) 和 [Spokenly](spokenly-alternative) 的免费版，都在你的 Mac 上运行语音模型。不上传，没有额度，断网也能用。代价是要下载一次模型，最好是 Apple Silicon 芯片的 Mac。

body: [闪电说](shandianshuo-alternative)、[豆包输入法](doubao-input-alternative)、[微信输入法](wechat-input-alternative)和[讯飞输入法](iflytek-input-alternative)也都能在 Mac 上语音输入。后三个本身是完整的拼音输入法，语音只是其中一个功能，用的时候得切换成它；豆包和微信的语音识别走云端。闪电说免费版带本地模型，高级功能按月收费。每一款的详细对比见下面的链接。

sections.heading: 怎么挑
body: 先看音频去哪儿：必须留在 Mac 上的话，只有本地应用符合。再看语言：中文，或者中英混说，优先选中文训练的模型。最后看价格和附加功能：AI 改写、手机应用和团队功能，是付费云端应用值这个价的地方。付一年钱之前，挑两个候选，用你平时真会说的话试一试。

faq.q: Mac 上最好用的免费语音输入软件是哪个？
faq.a: 取决于你的语言和隐私需求。免费的本地选择有 Superwhisper 免费版、Spokenly、Handy 和 TypeAloud；苹果自带听写不用安装，但一次只听一种语言，也不保留记录。

faq.q: 哪些 Mac 语音输入软件可以离线用？
faq.a: 本地运行的那些：VoiceInk、MacWhisper、TypeAloud，以及选了本地模型的 Superwhisper 或 Spokenly。Wispr Flow、Typeless、Aqua Voice、Willow Voice 这类云端应用需要联网。

faq.q: 中文识别哪个好？
faq.a: 看模型。Qwen3-ASR 和 SenseVoice 用大量中文训练，会边听边判断语言，这在夹英文时很重要；Whisper 则给整段录音定一种语言（[详情](whisper-chinese-english)）。挑两个候选，用你自己的句子试一试。

faq.q: 哪些语音输入软件支持 Intel Mac？
faq.a: 云端应用在支持的 Mac 上都能用。本地应用各不相同：有的要求 Apple Silicon，有的能在 Intel 上跑但更慢。看各应用的系统要求。

en.title: Wispr Flow vs Typeless (2026): price, free plan, offline, and a free option — TypeAloud
en.description: Wispr Flow and Typeless are both cloud dictation apps that rewrite your speech. How their prices, free plans and platforms compare, and a free local alternative.
heading: Wispr Flow or Typeless?
Same yearly price, double monthly.
en.intro: Wispr Flow and Typeless are the two best-known AI dictation apps. Both send your voice to the cloud, tidy it into writing and drop it at your cursor. Billed yearly, they cost the same. The differences are in monthly pricing, extras and platforms.

table.caption: Wispr Flow and Typeless compared
rows: Removes filler, adjusts tone per app
Turns rambling speech into clear writing, tone per app

sections.heading: Same idea, different emphasis
body: Wispr Flow leans towards work and teams: a meeting Notetaker, shared dictionaries and snippets, and higher tiers with SSO and HIPAA enforcement. Typeless leans into editing: it turns rambling speech into tidy prose, translates, has an Ask anything feature and a whisper mode for quiet rooms. Typeless also runs on Linux.

sections.heading: Price: equal yearly, very different monthly
body: Billed yearly, both Pro plans come to $144. Month to month, Wispr Flow is $15 and Typeless is $30, so a year of monthly billing costs $180 against $360. If you will not commit to a year, Wispr Flow costs half as much. Details: [Wispr Flow pricing](wispr-flow-pricing), [Typeless pricing](typeless-pricing).

sections.heading: What both have in common
body: Both need a connection, both send your audio to their servers, and both meter the free plan for that reason. If you want dictation that stays on your Mac, local apps are the other route; see [offline dictation](offline-dictation-mac) and the [roundup](best-dictation-apps-mac).

faq.q: Which is cheaper, Wispr Flow or Typeless?
faq.a: Billed yearly they cost the same, $12 a month. Month to month, Wispr Flow is $15 and Typeless is $30.

faq.q: Do Wispr Flow or Typeless work offline?
faq.a: No. Both transcribe in the cloud. For offline dictation you need a local app; see [offline dictation for Mac](offline-dictation-mac).

faq.q: Which is better for Chinese?
faq.a: Both list over 100 languages. We have no side-by-side test of their Chinese accuracy to quote. If you often mix Chinese and English in one sentence, see [mixed Chinese–English dictation](chinese-english-dictation).

faq.q: Is there a free alternative to both?
faq.a: Local dictation apps are free or one-time purchases; see [free dictation with no word limit](free-dictation-mac).

en.title: Wispr Flow vs Superwhisper (2026): cloud vs local, price, setup — TypeAloud
en.description: Wispr Flow rewrites in the cloud automatically; Superwhisper runs locally or in the cloud with modes you configure. Price, offline use and setup compared.
heading: Wispr Flow or Superwhisper?
Automatic, or configurable.
en.intro: Both put text at your cursor in any app. Wispr Flow does it one way, in the cloud, with AI cleanup switched on. Superwhisper lets you choose local or cloud models and build modes for each kind of writing. That choice decides most of the rest.

table.caption: Wispr Flow and Superwhisper compared
rows: Free plan; Pro $15/month, or $12/month billed annually ($144/year)
Local or cloud, depending on the model
Modes you configure: Voice, Message, Email, Super and custom

sections.heading: Automatic versus configurable
body: Wispr Flow has one behaviour: it cleans up what you say and matches the tone of the app you are in. There is little to set up. Superwhisper gives you modes, each with its own speech model, language model and instructions, and Super Mode reads the screen for context. That is powerful, and it means more choices to make before your first dictation.

sections.heading: Cloud versus local
body: Every Wispr Flow dictation goes to its servers. Superwhisper's free plan runs Whisper on your Mac with no word limit, and Pro adds both larger local models and cloud models. If you want dictation that works on a plane, only Superwhisper of the two does it.

sections.heading: What a year costs
body: Wispr Flow Pro is $144 a year billed annually. Superwhisper Pro is $84.99 a year, or $249.99 once, which pays for itself against the yearly plan in about three years. See [Wispr Flow pricing](wispr-flow-pricing).

sections.heading: Which to pick
body: Want it to just work and do not mind the cloud: Wispr Flow. Want local transcription, control over modes, or a one-time price: Superwhisper. If you want local without configuring modes, simpler local apps exist too; see [offline dictation](offline-dictation-mac).

faq.q: Which is cheaper, Wispr Flow or Superwhisper?
faq.a: Superwhisper. Its Pro is $84.99 a year against $144 for Wispr Flow, and its free plan has no word limit with local models.

faq.q: Does Superwhisper work offline?
faq.a: Yes, with local models. Wispr Flow does not; it transcribes in the cloud.

faq.q: Which is easier to set up?
faq.a: Wispr Flow. It has fewer settings and rewrites automatically. Superwhisper rewards time spent configuring modes.

faq.q: Is there a free option?
faq.a: Both have free plans. Other free local apps are listed in [free dictation with no word limit](free-dictation-mac).

en.title: Superwhisper vs MacWhisper (2026): dictation or transcription? — TypeAloud
en.description: Superwhisper is a dictation app; MacWhisper is a transcription app for recordings. Prices, system-wide dictation, file transcription and subtitles compared.
heading: Superwhisper or MacWhisper?
They answer different questions.
en.intro: The names are similar and both run Whisper on your Mac, so they get compared a lot. In practice Superwhisper is for speaking into the app you are using, and MacWhisper is for turning recordings into transcripts. Pick by which of those you do most.

table.caption: Superwhisper and MacWhisper compared
rows: Yes: Option+Space, text pasted at the cursor
Dictation types into the focused text field from a shortcut (version sold on macwhisper.com, not the App Store one); Pro adds Global, a floating window
Yes, in batches, with speaker labels

sections.heading: Dictation versus transcription
body: Superwhisper starts from a shortcut: press it in any text field, speak, press again, and the text is pasted where you were. Its modes can rewrite what you said into an email or message.

MacWhisper starts from a file: drop in an interview, lecture or meeting recording and get a transcript with speakers labelled, then export it as subtitles or a document. It also has dictation: a Dictation shortcut that types into the focused field (website version only) and, on Pro, Global, a floating window.

sections.heading: Which to pick
body: If you write by voice every day, Superwhisper. If you transcribe recordings, MacWhisper; its €64 one-time Pro is good value for that. Plenty of people use both.

sections.heading: If you only need one half
body: Only transcribe files? MacWhisper's free version covers the basics. Only dictate? Superwhisper's free tier runs local Whisper, and other free dictation apps exist; see [free dictation with no word limit](free-dictation-mac). For the difference between the two jobs, see [speech to text on Mac](mac-speech-to-text).

faq.q: Is MacWhisper a dictation app?
faq.a: Mainly it is a transcription app for files and meetings. It also has a Dictation feature that types into text fields (website version only) and, on Pro, a floating Global window.

sections.heading: Why the word cap disappears
body: Wispr Flow sends each recording to its servers, and every dictated word costs it compute. That is what [the weekly cap and the Pro plan](wispr-flow-pricing) pay for.

TypeAloud downloads a speech model once (Qwen3-ASR 0.6B, about 1 GB) and runs it on your Mac. After that, dictating 200 words or 20,000 words in a week costs nobody anything, so there is [no quota to enforce](free-dictation-mac).

sections.heading: The same hold, speak, release habit
body: Hold Ctrl+Shift in whatever app you are writing in, speak, and release. The text lands at your cursor: in your editor, your terminal, Slack, a browser field. Escape cancels a recording.
Finished transcripts are kept in History on your device. If a transcription fails and the audio was saved, you can retry it.

sections.heading: Where Wispr Flow is the better choice
body: Wispr Flow rewrites what you say: it drops filler words, fixes self-corrections and adjusts tone to the app you are in. TypeAloud gives you an accurate transcript of what you said and leaves the wording to you.
Wispr Flow also has iPhone and Android apps and team plans. TypeAloud is a desktop app, tested mainly on macOS. If you dictate on your phone or need shared team dictionaries, Wispr Flow fits better.

faq.q: Is TypeAloud really free?
faq.a: Yes. Local transcription needs no account, API key or subscription, and there is no word limit. Cloud transcription is optional and uses your own Groq or OpenAI key, which those providers may charge for.

faq.q: Does my audio leave my Mac?
faq.a: Not in local mode. The model runs on your device and transcripts are saved there. Audio is only uploaded if you choose a cloud engine with your own API key.

faq.q: Which Macs can run TypeAloud?
faq.a: TypeAloud runs on macOS 10.15 or later, on both Intel and Apple Silicon Macs. Local dictation is fastest on Apple Silicon. The recommended model is a one-time download of about 1 GB.

faq.q: Is there a Windows version?
faq.a: There are Windows and Linux builds, but they are experimental. macOS is the platform TypeAloud is tested on.

faq.q: Does Wispr Flow work offline?
faq.a: No. Wispr Flow transcribes on its servers, so it needs an internet connection. TypeAloud's local mode works with no connection after the model download; see [offline dictation for Mac](offline-dictation-mac).

faq.q: How much is Wispr Flow Pro?
faq.a: $15 a month, or $12 a month billed annually. The free plan allows 2,000 words a week on desktop. The [Wispr Flow pricing guide](wispr-flow-pricing) breaks down every plan.

faq.q: Is Wispr Flow better than Typeless?
faq.a: They are close: both are cloud apps that rewrite your speech. Wispr Flow is cheaper month to month; Typeless has a Linux app. See [Wispr Flow vs Typeless](wispr-flow-vs-typeless).

heading: A Typeless alternative
that works offline, for free.
en.intro: Typeless is a cloud voice keyboard with a weekly word limit on its free plan and a $12 to $30 monthly Pro plan. TypeAloud, a free dictation app for Mac, does the transcription on your Mac, so it is free, unlimited and still works with Wi-Fi off.

sections.heading: What you keep, what you give up
body: The core habit is the same in both apps: hold a shortcut, talk, and the text appears in the app you were already using. In TypeAloud the shortcut is Ctrl+Shift and the text is inserted at your cursor.
What Typeless adds is editing. It removes filler words, tidies repetition and formats lists for you. TypeAloud does not rewrite your speech, so what you get is a transcript of what you actually said.

sections.heading: Your dictation stays on your device
body: Typeless states that it keeps no cloud data after processing. Your audio still has to travel to a server to be transcribed. In TypeAloud's local mode the audio never leaves your Mac at all, which matters when you dictate client names, medical notes or unreleased work.
It also means dictation keeps working on a plane, on a train, or on a network that blocks cloud services.

sections.heading: Good with mixed Chinese and English
body: TypeAloud's local model is Qwen3-ASR, which detects the spoken language on its own. You can say a sentence that switches between Chinese and English without changing any setting first.

faq.q: Is TypeAloud a full replacement for Typeless?
faq.a: For dictating text into any Mac app, yes. It does not have Typeless's AI rewriting or its phone apps.

faq.q: How much does TypeAloud cost?
faq.a: Nothing. Local transcription has no subscription and no word limit. An optional cloud mode uses your own Groq or OpenAI API key.

faq.q: Do I need to sign up?
faq.a: No. Download the app, pick a local model and start dictating. There is no account.

faq.q: What does it need to run?
faq.a: A Mac, ideally with Apple Silicon, about 1 GB for the recommended model, plus microphone and Accessibility permissions.

faq.q: How much is Typeless Pro?
faq.a: $30 a month, or $12 a month if you pay for a year up front. See [Typeless pricing](typeless-pricing) for what each plan includes.

faq.q: Does Typeless work offline?
faq.a: Its transcription and editing run in the cloud, and its own FAQ says core features work best with an internet connection. TypeAloud's local mode needs no connection.

faq.q: Typeless or Wispr Flow?
faq.a: Both are cloud apps that tidy your speech into writing. Compare them in [Wispr Flow vs Typeless](wispr-flow-vs-typeless).

en.title: Free, open-source Superwhisper alternative for Mac — TypeAloud
en.description: TypeAloud is a free, open-source Superwhisper alternative: local dictation on your Mac with no Pro plan and no account, built for sentences that mix Chinese and English.
heading: A Superwhisper alternative
with nothing behind a Pro plan.
en.intro: Superwhisper's free plan already runs Whisper on your Mac. Its Pro plan, at $8.49 a month, $84.99 a year or $249.99 once, adds AI modes, cloud models and more local models. TypeAloud is a dictation app for Mac that is free and open source, with no paid tier, and its local model is Qwen3-ASR instead of Whisper.

sections.heading: Both are local. The model is the difference.
body: Superwhisper's free plan and TypeAloud both transcribe on your Mac with no word limit, so price alone does not decide it. What you dictate does.

TypeAloud runs Qwen3-ASR, which works out the language from the audio itself. A sentence that starts in Chinese and switches to English halfway is written down as you said it, with no language setting to change first. [Whisper picks one language per recording](whisper-chinese-english), and [mixed sentences](chinese-english-dictation) are where it slips most often.

sections.heading: Every feature is in the free app
body: There is no Pro plan to unlock. The larger Qwen3-ASR 1.7B model (about 2.52 GB), the dictionary and automatic replacements, History with retry for failed transcriptions, and the optional cloud mode with your own Groq or OpenAI key all come with the free app; the models download from inside it.
The source is on GitHub under GPL-3.0, so you can check exactly what happens to your audio.

sections.heading: Where Superwhisper is the better choice
body: Superwhisper's Pro modes rewrite what you say into an email, a message or your own format, and Super Mode adapts to what is on screen. TypeAloud gives you a faithful transcript and leaves the wording to you.
Superwhisper also records meetings, transcribes audio files and has iPhone and Android apps. If you need those, or want your speech turned into finished prose, Superwhisper fits better.

faq.q: Is TypeAloud free in the same way as Superwhisper's free plan?
faq.a: TypeAloud has no paid plan at all. Local transcription, both Qwen3-ASR model sizes and every feature are free. Optional cloud transcription uses your own Groq or OpenAI key, which those providers may charge for.

faq.q: Can I still use Whisper?
faq.a: Not as a local model. Locally TypeAloud runs Qwen3-ASR. Whisper is available through the optional cloud mode, with your own Groq or OpenAI API key.

faq.q: Does my audio leave my Mac?
faq.a: Not in local mode. The model runs on your device and transcripts are saved there. Audio is only uploaded if you choose a cloud engine with your own API key.

faq.q: Which Macs can run TypeAloud?
faq.a: TypeAloud runs on macOS 10.15 or later, on both Intel and Apple Silicon Macs. Local dictation is fastest on Apple Silicon. The recommended model is a one-time download of about 1 GB.

faq.q: Superwhisper or Wispr Flow?
faq.a: Superwhisper can run locally and lets you configure modes; Wispr Flow is cloud-only and rewrites automatically. See [Wispr Flow vs Superwhisper](wispr-flow-vs-superwhisper).

faq.q: Can Superwhisper transcribe audio files like MacWhisper?
faq.a: File transcription is part of Superwhisper Pro, but MacWhisper is the specialist for recordings. See [Superwhisper vs MacWhisper](superwhisper-vs-macwhisper).

en.title: Free VoiceInk alternative for Mac — TypeAloud
en.description: TypeAloud is a free VoiceInk alternative: open-source local dictation for Mac with no licence to buy, no device limit and Qwen3-ASR for mixed Chinese–English.
heading: A VoiceInk alternative
free, with no per-device licence.
en.intro: VoiceInk is a well-made local dictation app for Mac, sold as a one-time licence from $25 for one Mac. TypeAloud is a dictation app that also transcribes on your Mac and is open source, but it is free and has no device limit.

sections.heading: Same idea, different speech model
body: Both apps keep your voice on your Mac: hold a shortcut, speak, and the text lands at your cursor. In TypeAloud the shortcut is Ctrl+Shift, and a double tap records hands-free until the next press.

The difference is the model underneath. VoiceInk lets you choose from many local models, including Parakeet, [Whisper](whisper-chinese-english), Nemotron and SenseVoice, and check each one's languages. TypeAloud ships a single default tuned for Chinese, English and both mixed: Qwen3-ASR, which detects the language from the audio and handles a sentence that moves between Chinese and English without a setting change.

sections.heading: No licence to count
body: VoiceInk's licences are per device: one, two or three Macs. TypeAloud is free, so a work Mac, a home Mac and an old laptop cost the same as one. It also has Windows and Linux builds, though those are still experimental.

sections.heading: Where VoiceInk is the better choice
body: VoiceInk can clean up what you say with an AI pass, on the Mac or through a provider, removing filler words and formatting text, and it can rewrite selected text from a spoken instruction. TypeAloud gives you a faithful transcript and leaves the wording to you.
VoiceInk also has an iOS app and a large community behind it. If you want a wide choice of models and AI cleanup that can run on your Mac, VoiceInk is worth its price.

faq.q: Is TypeAloud really free?
faq.a: Yes. Local transcription needs no account, API key, licence or subscription, and there is no word limit. Cloud transcription is optional and uses your own Groq or OpenAI key, which those providers may charge for.

faq.q: Are both apps open source?
faq.a: Yes. Both publish their source under the GPL-3.0 licence. TypeAloud's signed builds are free; VoiceInk sells signed builds from $25.

faq.q: Does my audio leave my Mac?
faq.a: Not in local mode. The model runs on your device and transcripts are saved there. Audio is only uploaded if you choose a cloud engine with your own API key.

faq.q: Which Macs can run TypeAloud?
faq.a: TypeAloud runs on macOS 10.15 or later, on both Intel and Apple Silicon Macs. Local dictation is fastest on Apple Silicon. The recommended model is a one-time download of about 1 GB.

sections.heading: Where MacWhisper is the better choice

faq.q: Can MacWhisper type into other apps?
faq.a: Yes. Its Dictation feature types into the focused text field, in the version sold on macwhisper.com; Pro adds Global, a floating transcription window. Its focus is still transcribing files.

faq.q: Can TypeAloud transcribe audio files?
faq.a: No. TypeAloud is for live dictation. For files, MacWhisper is the better tool.

faq.q: Is TypeAloud really free?

en.title: Voice prompts for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex: how to dictate well — TypeAloud
en.description: How to dictate prompts to AI coding agents: how to structure a spoken prompt, which dictation tools work in terminals and editors, and how to handle identifiers.
heading: Talking to your coding agent:
how to dictate prompts well.
en.intro: Working with Claude Code, Cursor or Codex means writing long instructions in plain language, which is exactly what speech is good at. Dictating prompts well takes a little structure, the right tool for where you type, and a plan for identifiers that speech gets wrong.

sections.heading: Why speaking prompts pays off
body: A useful prompt explains what is wrong, what you tried and what done looks like. That is prose, not code. Most people speak at around 130 words a minute and type at around 40.

sections.heading: Structure a spoken prompt
body: Speak in four parts: the goal ("make the login form validate email"), the context (which files, what the error says), the constraints ("don't change the API"), and what done looks like ("tests pass, no new dependencies"). Then read it once and fix names before sending.
Dictate, don't edit, while you talk. Corrections are faster with the keyboard afterwards.

sections.heading: Tools that work where you type
body: Claude Code has built-in dictation: run `/voice`, then hold Space to record and release to insert the text, or use `/voice tap` to start and stop with single taps. It needs a Claude.ai sign-in, streams audio to Anthropic's servers for transcription, does not work over SSH, and supports 20 languages, which do not include Chinese. It only works inside Claude Code.
macOS Dictation works in Terminal, iTerm and editors, with its usual limits: one language at a time and a stop after 30 seconds of silence.

System-wide dictation apps put text at the cursor in any app, so one shortcut covers the agent, the editor and chat. Cloud options include [Wispr Flow](wispr-flow-alternative); local ones include [Superwhisper](superwhisper-alternative), [VoiceInk](voiceink-alternative) and TypeAloud, which we make. More in [dictating into any app](dictate-into-apps).

sections.heading: Identifiers, paths and jargon
body: Speech engines are poor at camelCase, snake_case, file paths and flags. Speak the intent and type the exact names. Most dictation apps have a dictionary or replacement list; add the project, library and service names you say every day. Some ship with common tech terms built in.
If you explain code in Chinese and name things in English, choose a tool that [handles mixed Chinese–English](chinese-english-dictation).

sections.heading: Private code
body: Cloud dictation uploads your audio, which may include client names and unreleased features. If that matters, use on-device Dictation or a local app; see [private dictation](private-dictation).

faq.q: Does Claude Code support voice input?
faq.a: Yes, through `/voice`: hold Space to dictate into the prompt. It needs a Claude.ai sign-in, transcribes in the cloud and does not support Chinese. For other apps you need system or third-party dictation.

faq.q: Does macOS Dictation work in the terminal?
faq.a: Yes. It types into the focused text field, including Terminal and iTerm.

faq.q: How do I dictate code identifiers?
faq.a: Type them, or add the ones you repeat to a dictation app's dictionary or replacement list.

faq.q: Is voice faster than typing for prompts?
faq.a: For explanations, usually: speech runs around three times faster than typing. For short commands, typing is often quicker.

heading: 对编程助手说话：
怎么把提示词说好。
zh.intro: 用 Claude Code、Cursor 或 Codex 干活，就是用自然语言写很长的指令，这正是说话擅长的事。把提示词说好，需要一点结构、一个在你打字的地方能用的工具，以及处理变量名这类语音容易出错内容的办法。

sections.heading: 为什么值得用说的
body: 好的提示词要讲清楚哪里有问题、试过什么、做到什么程度算完成。这是一段段文字，不是代码。多数人说话每分钟约 130 个英文词，打字约 40 个。

sections.heading: 口述提示词的结构
body: 按四部分说：目标（“让登录表单校验邮箱格式”）、背景（涉及哪些文件、报错信息是什么）、约束（“不要改接口”）、完成标准（“测试通过，不加新依赖”）。说完通读一遍，改好名字再发出去。
说的时候只管说，别边说边改，事后用键盘改更快。

sections.heading: 在你打字的地方能用的工具
body: Claude Code 有自带的语音听写：运行 `/voice`，然后按住空格录音，松开后插入文字；也可以用 `/voice tap` 改成点一下开始、再点一下结束。它需要登录 Claude.ai 账号，音频发到 Anthropic 的服务器转写，SSH 会话里用不了，支持 20 种语言，但不包括中文。它只在 Claude Code 里有效。
macOS 自带听写在 Terminal、iTerm 和编辑器里都能用，限制照旧：一次一种语言，30 秒没声音就停。

系统级的听写应用能把文字放到任意应用的光标处，一个快捷键覆盖编程助手、编辑器和聊天。云端的有 [Wispr Flow](wispr-flow-alternative)；本地的有 [Superwhisper](superwhisper-alternative)、[VoiceInk](voiceink-alternative)，以及我们做的 TypeAloud。详见[在各应用里语音输入](dictate-into-apps)。

sections.heading: 变量名、路径和术语
body: 语音识别对 camelCase、snake_case、文件路径和命令参数都不擅长。意图用说的，精确的名字用打的。多数听写应用有词典或替换列表，把你每天都会说的项目名、库名和服务名加进去；有些应用还内置了常见技术词。
如果你讲代码用中文、起名用英文，选一个[能处理中英混说](chinese-english-dictation)的工具。

sections.heading: 私有代码
body: 云端听写会上传你的录音，里面可能有客户名和没发布的功能。在意的话，用设备端的系统听写或本地应用，见[不上传录音的语音输入](private-dictation)。

faq.q: Claude Code 支持语音输入吗？
faq.a: 支持，通过 `/voice`：按住空格往输入框里听写。需要登录 Claude.ai 账号，在云端转写，不支持中文。其他应用需要系统听写或第三方工具。

faq.q: macOS 听写在终端里能用吗？
faq.a: 能。它会输入到当前获得焦点的输入框，包括 Terminal 和 iTerm。

faq.q: 代码里的变量名怎么口述？
faq.a: 直接打字，或者把反复用到的名字加进听写应用的词典或替换列表。

faq.q: 用语音写提示词真的比打字快吗？
faq.a: 写说明类的内容通常是，说话大约比打字快三倍。短命令往往还是打字更快。

en.title: Open-source dictation apps for Mac, compared — TypeAloud
en.description: Open-source dictation apps you can run on a Mac: licences, speech models, prices and what open source lets you check. Handy, VoiceInk, TypeAloud and more.
heading: Open-source dictation for Mac:
what is out there.
en.intro: A dictation app processes everything you say while it records, so being able to read its code is worth something. Several open-source dictation apps run on a Mac. They differ in licence, in the speech models they use and in whether the ready-made builds are free.

table.caption: Open-source dictation apps for Mac
rows: Several, including Whisper, Parakeet and SenseVoice
Many, including Parakeet, Whisper and SenseVoice

sections.heading: What open source lets you check
body: With the source public you can see what an app records, where the audio goes, what it stores and which network requests it makes. For a privacy claim like "local mode never uploads audio", that is the difference between trusting and checking.

sections.heading: Free builds versus building it yourself
body: Open source does not always mean free downloads. VoiceInk's code is GPL-3.0, and its signed builds are sold; you can build it yourself from source. Handy and TypeAloud offer free signed builds.

sections.heading: How to choose
body: Pick by language first. Whisper and Parakeet are strong in English and European languages; for Chinese, and especially Chinese mixed with English, look for a model trained on a lot of Chinese, such as SenseVoice or Qwen3-ASR ([why](whisper-chinese-english)), and test it with your own speech.
Then look at activity: the date of the last release, how quickly issues get answered, and whether macOS updates are kept up with.

sections.heading: Engines, not apps
body: If you are a developer, the engines underneath are open source too: whisper.cpp and llama.cpp run speech models on a Mac, and you can call them from your own scripts. See [running Qwen3-ASR on a Mac](qwen3-asr-mac).

faq.q: Is there a free open-source dictation app for Mac?
faq.a: Yes. Handy and TypeAloud are open source with free builds; VoiceInk is open source with paid builds.

faq.q: Is open-source dictation private?
faq.a: Open source lets you check. Local transcription is what keeps audio on your Mac; read the code or test offline to confirm.

faq.q: Which open-source option is best for Chinese?
faq.a: One with a Chinese-trained model, such as SenseVoice or Qwen3-ASR.

faq.q: Can I build these myself?
faq.a: Yes, all three publish build instructions in their repositories.

zh.title: Mac 开源语音输入软件有哪些？许可证、模型和价格对比 — TypeAloud
zh.description: 能在 Mac 上用的开源语音输入应用：许可证、语音模型、价格，以及开源能让你核实什么。Handy、VoiceInk、TypeAloud 等。
heading: Mac 上的开源语音输入，
有哪些可选。
zh.intro: 语音输入应用会处理你录音时说的每一句话，所以能看到它的代码是有价值的。能在 Mac 上用的开源听写应用有好几个，区别在许可证、用的语音模型，以及现成的安装包是否免费。

table.caption: Mac 开源语音输入应用
rows: 多种，包括 Whisper、Parakeet 和 SenseVoice
多种，包括 Parakeet、Whisper 和 SenseVoice

sections.heading: 开源能让你核实什么
body: 源代码公开，你就能看到应用录了什么、音频发到哪里、存了什么、发出了哪些网络请求。对“本地模式不上传录音”这样的隐私承诺来说，这是“相信”和“核实”的区别。

sections.heading: 免费安装包和自己编译
body: 开源不一定等于免费下载。VoiceInk 的代码是 GPL-3.0，签名安装包是收费的，你也可以自己从源码编译。Handy 和 TypeAloud 提供免费的签名安装包。

sections.heading: 怎么选
body: 先按语言选。Whisper 和 Parakeet 擅长英文和欧洲语言；中文，尤其是中英混说，找用大量中文训练的模型，比如 SenseVoice 或 Qwen3-ASR（[原因](whisper-chinese-english)），再用你自己的话测一测。
再看活跃度：最近一次发布是什么时候、问题回复得快不快、有没有跟上 macOS 的更新。

sections.heading: 底层引擎也是开源的
body: 如果你是开发者，底层引擎同样开源：whisper.cpp 和 llama.cpp 都能在 Mac 上运行语音模型，可以在你自己的脚本里调用。见[在 Mac 上运行 Qwen3-ASR](qwen3-asr-mac)。

faq.q: 有免费的 Mac 开源语音输入应用吗？
faq.a: 有。Handy 和 TypeAloud 开源且安装包免费；VoiceInk 开源，安装包付费。

faq.q: 开源的语音输入就一定私密吗？
faq.a: 开源让你能核实。真正让录音留在 Mac 上的是本地转写，看代码或者断网测试一下就能确认。

faq.q: 中文用哪个开源方案好？
faq.a: 选带中文训练模型的，比如 SenseVoice 或 Qwen3-ASR。

faq.q: 能自己编译吗？
faq.a: 能，三者都在仓库里写了编译方法。

en.title: How to run Qwen3-ASR on a Mac: Python, MLX, llama.cpp and apps — TypeAloud
en.description: Ways to run Alibaba's Qwen3-ASR speech model on a Mac: the official qwen-asr package, MLX ports, llama.cpp, and ready-made apps. With speed and memory figures from an M4.
heading: Running Qwen3-ASR on a Mac,
four ways.
en.intro: Qwen3-ASR is Alibaba's open speech recognition model. It covers 52 languages and dialects, 22 of them Chinese dialects, detects the language on its own and handles sentences that mix languages. The official instructions assume an NVIDIA GPU; on a Mac you have four routes, from Python to ready-made apps.

table.caption: Qwen3-ASR in TypeAloud, measured on an M4 with 24 GB

sections.heading: 1. The official qwen-asr package
body: Alibaba publishes a Python package: `pip install -U qwen-asr`, then load `Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B` or 1.7B and call `transcribe()`. Pass `language=None` for automatic detection, or a language name to force one. The model card's examples target NVIDIA GPUs (CUDA), so on a Mac this is the least direct route.

sections.heading: 2. MLX: the most direct route
body: mlx-qwen3-asr is an Apache-2.0 reimplementation of Qwen3-ASR for Apple's MLX framework, so it runs natively on Apple Silicon (M1 to M4). With Python 3.10 or later:

`pip install mlx-qwen3-asr`, then `brew install ffmpeg` if your audio is not WAV, then `mlx-qwen3-asr audio.wav` prints the transcript. In Python: `from mlx_qwen3_asr import transcribe`, then `transcribe("audio.wav").text`.
It splits long recordings at quiet points into 30-second chunks by itself. The 0.6B model needs about 1.2 GB of memory and 1.7B about 3.4 GB.

sections.heading: 3. llama.cpp
body: llama.cpp lists Qwen3-ASR among its supported audio models, with ready-made files at `ggml-org/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B-GGUF` and `ggml-org/Qwen3-ASR-1.7B-GGUF`. Install it with `brew install llama.cpp`; `llama-mtmd-cli -hf ggml-org/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B-GGUF` downloads both the model and the audio projector (mmproj) it needs. llama.cpp's multimodal documentation covers passing audio. On Apple Silicon it uses Metal, and 8-bit (Q8_0) files are about half the size of the originals.

sections.heading: 4. Ready-made apps
body: If you want dictation rather than code, some Mac apps bundle Qwen3-ASR. Qwen Scribe offers file transcription and system-wide dictation on Apple Silicon; Echosy transcribes files and dictates system-wide, with a free tier that includes Qwen3-ASR 0.6B (15-minute sessions) and a one-time $49.80 Pro that adds 1.7B and Whisper; and TypeAloud, which we make, uses it for free dictation into any app. The table above is from our measurements of TypeAloud's llama.cpp setup on an M4.

sections.heading: 0.6B or 1.7B?
body: 0.6B is roughly twice as fast and needs about half the memory. In our M4 measurements, 1.7B took a little over twice as long to transcribe. Whether it is more accurate on everyday dictation is something to test with your own speech; start with 0.6B.

sections.heading: Long audio
body: Qwen3-ASR is built around clips rather than hours of audio, so tools split long recordings: mlx-qwen3-asr cuts at quiet points into 30-second chunks, and dictation apps do the same while you speak (TypeAloud uses pieces of 20 to 75 seconds). If you call the model directly through Python or llama.cpp, split long files at pauses yourself.

faq.q: Can Qwen3-ASR run on a Mac?
faq.a: Yes, through MLX ports, llama.cpp or apps that bundle it. The official Python examples target NVIDIA GPUs.

faq.q: Does Qwen3-ASR need a language setting?
faq.a: No. Pass `language=None` for automatic detection, or a language name to force one.

faq.q: How much memory does it need?
faq.a: In our M4 measurements, 0.6B peaked at about 1.4 GB and 1.7B at about 2.9 GB.

faq.q: Is Qwen3-ASR good at Chinese?
faq.a: It covers Mandarin, Cantonese and 22 Chinese dialects, and handles mixed Chinese–English. Test with your own speech; see [mixed Chinese–English dictation](chinese-english-dictation).

zh.title: 在 Mac 上运行 Qwen3-ASR 的四种方法：Python、MLX、llama.cpp、现成应用 — TypeAloud
zh.description: 在 Mac 上运行阿里 Qwen3-ASR 语音识别模型的几种办法：官方 qwen-asr 包、MLX 移植版、llama.cpp，以及现成的应用。附 M4 上的速度和内存数据。
heading: 在 Mac 上跑 Qwen3-ASR，
四种方法。
zh.intro: Qwen3-ASR 是阿里开源的语音识别模型，支持 52 种语言和方言（其中 22 种是中文方言），能自动判断语言，也能处理中英混说。官方教程默认你有 NVIDIA 显卡；在 Mac 上有四条路，从写 Python 到直接用现成应用。

table.caption: TypeAloud 中的 Qwen3-ASR，M4 / 24 GB 实测

sections.heading: 1. 官方 qwen-asr 包
body: 阿里发布了 Python 包：`pip install -U qwen-asr`，然后加载 `Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B` 或 1.7B，调用 `transcribe()`。传 `language=None` 自动检测语言，也可以传语言名强制指定。模型卡里的示例针对 NVIDIA 显卡（CUDA），所以在 Mac 上这是最绕的一条路。

sections.heading: 2. MLX：最直接的路
body: mlx-qwen3-asr 是用苹果 MLX 框架重新实现的 Qwen3-ASR，Apache-2.0 协议，可以在 Apple Silicon（M1 到 M4）上原生运行。需要 Python 3.10 或更新版本：
先 `pip install mlx-qwen3-asr`；音频不是 WAV 的话再 `brew install ffmpeg`；然后 `mlx-qwen3-asr audio.wav` 就会输出转写结果。在 Python 里：`from mlx_qwen3_asr import transcribe`，再 `transcribe("audio.wav").text`。
它会自动在安静处把长录音切成 30 秒的片段。0.6B 模型约需 1.2 GB 内存，1.7B 约需 3.4 GB。

sections.heading: 3. llama.cpp
body: llama.cpp 把 Qwen3-ASR 列在支持的音频模型里，提供现成的文件：`ggml-org/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B-GGUF` 和 `ggml-org/Qwen3-ASR-1.7B-GGUF`。用 `brew install llama.cpp` 安装，`llama-mtmd-cli -hf ggml-org/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B-GGUF` 会同时下载模型和它需要的音频投影文件（mmproj）。怎么传入音频见 llama.cpp 的多模态文档。在 Apple Silicon 上它用 Metal 加速，8 位（Q8_0）文件约为原版一半大小。

sections.heading: 4. 现成的应用
body: 如果你要的是语音输入而不是写代码，有些 Mac 应用内置了 Qwen3-ASR。Qwen Scribe 在 Apple Silicon 上提供文件转写和系统级听写；Echosy 能转写文件、也能系统级听写，免费版包含 Qwen3-ASR 0.6B（每次 15 分钟），一次性 49.8 美元的 Pro 加上 1.7B 和 Whisper；我们做的 TypeAloud 用它在任意应用里免费听写。上面的表格是我们在 M4 上实测 TypeAloud 的 llama.cpp 方案得到的数据。

sections.heading: 0.6B 还是 1.7B
body: 0.6B 大约快一倍，内存只要一半左右。我们在 M4 上的实测里，1.7B 的转写时间是 0.6B 的两倍多。它在日常听写中是否更准，要用你自己的话测；建议先用 0.6B。

sections.heading: 长音频
body: Qwen3-ASR 是按片段而不是按几小时的长音频设计的，所以各种工具都会切分长录音：mlx-qwen3-asr 在安静处切成 30 秒的片段，听写应用也是边说边切（TypeAloud 切成 20 到 75 秒）。如果你直接通过 Python 或 llama.cpp 调用模型，长文件要自己在停顿处切开。

faq.q: Qwen3-ASR 能在 Mac 上跑吗？
faq.a: 能，通过 MLX 移植版、llama.cpp 或内置它的应用。官方 Python 示例针对 NVIDIA 显卡。

faq.q: Qwen3-ASR 要设置语言吗？
faq.a: 不用。传 `language=None` 会自动检测，也可以传语言名强制指定。

faq.q: 需要多少内存？
faq.a: 我们在 M4 上实测，0.6B 峰值约 1.4 GB，1.7B 约 2.9 GB。

faq.q: Qwen3-ASR 中文好吗？
faq.a: 它支持普通话、粤语和 22 种中文方言，也能处理中英混说。最好用你自己的话测一测，见[中英混合语音输入](chinese-english-dictation)。

en.title: Whisper and mixed Chinese–English speech: why it fails and what works — TypeAloud
en.description: Whisper settles on one language for a recording, so sentences that switch between Chinese and English often come out wrong. Why it happens, workarounds, and models built for mixed speech.
heading: Why Whisper garbles
mixed Chinese and English.
en.intro: Say "帮我 review 一下这个 pull request" to a Whisper-based dictation app and you may get the English words spelled out in Chinese characters, dropped, or the whole sentence turned into English. This page explains why, what you can try, and which models handle it properly.

sections.heading: One language for the whole recording
body: Unless you set a language, standard Whisper listens to the first 30 seconds, decides which language you are speaking, and transcribes the rest in that language. A sentence that switches languages halfway tends to get pushed towards the one it chose, which shows up as dropped words, English spelled out in Chinese characters, or a translation. How bad it gets depends on the model size and the app's settings.

Its vocabulary is shared across languages and most of its training audio is in a single language, so switching mid-sentence is exactly the case it saw least. Research on Whisper and code-switching describes errors clustering at the switch points.

sections.heading: Workarounds if you stay with Whisper
body: Set the language to Chinese rather than letting it detect, so short English words do not flip the whole window into English.

If your app has a prompt or vocabulary setting (Whisper calls it the initial prompt), write a sentence in Simplified Chinese there that includes the English terms you use, such as product names. That nudges Whisper to keep them in Latin letters and to write Simplified rather than Traditional characters.

For developers: fine-tuning on mixed Chinese–English data helps most. Published work using small adapters on top of Whisper reports clear gains on mixed speech, but that is a research project, not a setting.

sections.heading: Use a model trained for it
body: Newer speech models trained heavily on Chinese handle switching natively. Qwen3-ASR detects the language from the audio and covers 22 Chinese dialects; SenseVoice is another option. Both can run on a Mac: through Python or MLX if you code ([how](qwen3-asr-mac)), or through apps such as Handy and TypeAloud, which we make. More in [mixed Chinese–English dictation](chinese-english-dictation).

faq.q: Does Whisper support Chinese?
faq.a: Yes. It transcribes Mandarin well when you speak only Chinese. The problem is switching languages within a sentence.

faq.q: Why does Whisper output Traditional Chinese?
faq.a: Its training data mixes Simplified and Traditional text. An initial prompt written in Simplified Chinese usually steers it to Simplified.

faq.q: Which dictation apps use Whisper?
faq.a: Many local Mac apps, including [Superwhisper](superwhisper-alternative), [VoiceInk](voiceink-alternative) and [MacWhisper](macwhisper-alternative), offer Whisper models.

faq.q: Is there a free app that handles mixed speech?
faq.a: Apps built on Chinese-trained models, such as Handy with SenseVoice or TypeAloud with Qwen3-ASR, are free and run locally.

zh.title: Whisper 中英混合识别不准？原因、解决办法和替代模型 — TypeAloud
zh.description: Whisper 通常给整段录音定一种语言，中英夹杂的句子就容易出错，还常输出繁体。原因、可以试的办法，以及能处理中英混说的模型。
heading: Whisper 为什么
听不准中英混说。
zh.intro: 对着基于 Whisper 的听写应用说"帮我 review 一下这个 pull request"，你可能会得到被写成汉字音译的英文、被吞掉的英文，或者整句被翻成英文。这一页讲清楚原因、能试的办法，以及哪些模型能正确处理。

sections.heading: 整段录音，一种语言
body: 如果你没指定语言，标准的 Whisper 会听开头最多 30 秒，判断你说的是哪种语言，然后整段都按这种语言转写。半句中文半句英文的话，容易被推向它选定的那种，表现为漏词、英文被写成汉字音译，或者被翻译。严重程度取决于模型大小和应用的设置。
它的词表是所有语言共用的，训练音频大多是单一语言，所以句中切换语言正是它见得最少的情况。关于 Whisper 语码转换的研究也发现，错误集中出现在语言切换的位置。

sections.heading: 继续用 Whisper 的话可以试试
body: 把语言设成中文，不要让它自动检测，这样几个英文单词不会把整个窗口带成英文。
如果你用的应用有“提示词”或“词汇”设置（Whisper 里叫 initial prompt），在里面写一句简体中文，把常用的英文词（比如产品名）放进去，可以让 Whisper 保留英文拼写，并输出简体而不是繁体。
面向开发者：效果最好的是用中英混合数据微调。已有研究在 Whisper 上加小型适配器，中英混说的识别明显变好，但那是研究项目，不是一个设置项。

sections.heading: 换一个为此训练的模型
body: 大量用中文训练的新一代语音模型原生就能处理语言切换。Qwen3-ASR 直接从声音里判断语言，还覆盖 22 种中文方言；SenseVoice 是另一个选择。两者都能在 Mac 上运行：会写代码的话可以用 Python 或 MLX（[方法](qwen3-asr-mac)），也可以通过 Handy，或者我们做的 TypeAloud 这类应用。更多见[中英混合语音输入](chinese-english-dictation)。

faq.q: Whisper 支持中文吗？
faq.a: 支持。只说中文时，它的普通话识别不错。问题出在一句话里切换语言。

faq.q: Whisper 为什么输出繁体？
faq.a: 它的训练数据里简体和繁体混在一起。用简体中文写 initial prompt，通常就能让它输出简体。

faq.q: 哪些听写应用用的是 Whisper？
faq.a: 很多 Mac 本地应用都提供 Whisper 模型，包括 [Superwhisper](superwhisper-alternative)、[VoiceInk](voiceink-alternative) 和 [MacWhisper](macwhisper-alternative)。

faq.q: 有能处理中英混说的免费应用吗？
faq.a: 基于中文训练模型的应用，比如用 SenseVoice 的 Handy、用 Qwen3-ASR 的 TypeAloud，都免费并在本地运行。

en.title: How to voice type on a Mac: three ways, step by step — TypeAloud
en.description: Turn on macOS Dictation, use Voice Control, or install a dictation app. Step-by-step instructions for each, with what each one is good at.
en.nav: How to voice type on a Mac
heading: How to voice type on a Mac,
three ways.
en.intro: You can type with your voice on any recent Mac without installing anything. Built-in Dictation covers short text, Voice Control covers controlling the Mac by voice, and a separate dictation app adds things like a history of what you said and mixed-language sentences. Here is how to set up each.

sections.heading: 1. Built-in Dictation
body: Open System Settings, click Keyboard, go to Dictation and turn it on. Pick a shortcut from the Shortcut menu, or press the Microphone key if your keyboard has one. Under Languages, click Edit to add the languages you speak, and under Microphone source choose your microphone instead of Automatic if Dictation picks the wrong one.

To dictate, put the cursor in a text field, press the shortcut and speak. Press it again, or Escape, to stop. Dictation also ends by itself after 30 seconds without speech. Auto-punctuation works in supported languages.

sections.heading: 2. Voice Control
body: Voice Control, in System Settings > Accessibility > Voice Control, lets you run the whole Mac by voice: open apps, click buttons, and dictate and edit text with commands like "select previous word". Turn it on and wait for its language files to download. Then speak into a text field to type; say "go to sleep" to pause listening and "wake up" to resume.
It is built for people who cannot easily use a keyboard or mouse. While it is on, standard Dictation is unavailable, so turn it off again if you only want method 1.

sections.heading: 3. A third-party dictation app
body: A third-party app is worth it when you write paragraphs rather than sentences, mix languages, or want a record of what you said. Options include [Superwhisper](superwhisper-alternative), [VoiceInk](voiceink-alternative), [Wispr Flow](wispr-flow-alternative) and TypeAloud, which we make; the [roundup](best-dictation-apps-mac) compares them.

Setup is similar for all of them: install the app, grant microphone permission and macOS Accessibility permission (which lets an app type into other apps), then either download a speech model or sign in, depending on whether the app is local or cloud. After that you press or hold the app's shortcut and speak.

sections.heading: Which to use
body: Replying to a message or searching: built-in Dictation. Controlling the Mac without your hands: Voice Control. Writing documents, prompts or notes by voice: a dictation app. If built-in Dictation misbehaves, see [Mac dictation not working](mac-dictation-not-working).

faq.q: What is the shortcut for dictation on a Mac?
faq.a: You choose it in System Settings > Keyboard > Dictation > Shortcut, or press the Microphone key if your keyboard has one. Third-party apps each have their own shortcut.

faq.q: Can I dictate in Chinese on a Mac?
faq.a: Yes. Add Mandarin under Keyboard > Dictation > Languages. Built-in Dictation uses one language at a time; for sentences that mix Chinese and English, see [mixed Chinese–English dictation](chinese-english-dictation).

faq.q: Does Mac dictation work offline?
faq.a: Keyboard settings show whether general dictation is processed on your device. See [offline dictation on Mac](offline-dictation-mac) for other options.

faq.q: How do I turn off dictation on a Mac?
faq.a: Turn Dictation off in System Settings > Keyboard > Dictation. If Voice Control is on, turn it off under Accessibility.

zh.title: Mac 怎么语音输入？三种方法，一步一步设置 — TypeAloud
zh.description: 打开 macOS 自带听写、使用语音控制，或者装一个语音输入应用。每种方法的设置步骤，以及各自适合做什么。
heading: Mac 怎么语音输入，
三种方法。
zh.intro: 在较新的 Mac 上，不装任何东西也能用语音打字。系统自带的听写适合短句，语音控制适合用声音操作整台 Mac，单独的语音输入应用则多了历史记录、中英混说这些功能。下面是每种方法的设置步骤。

sections.heading: 1. 系统自带的听写
body: 打开“系统设置”，点“键盘”，找到“听写”并打开。在“快捷键”菜单里选一个快捷键；键盘上有麦克风键的话也可以直接按它。在“语言”旁边点“编辑”，加上普通话等你要说的语言；如果听写选错了麦克风，在“麦克风来源”里手动选，不要用“自动”。
听写时把光标放进输入框，按快捷键说话，再按一次或按 Esc 结束。30 秒没检测到语音时听写也会自动结束。支持的语言会自动加标点。

sections.heading: 2. 语音控制
body: “系统设置 > 辅助功能 > 语音控制”可以用声音操作整台 Mac：打开应用、点按钮，也能用“选择上一个词”这类口令听写和编辑文字。打开它，等语言文件下载完，然后在输入框里直接说话就能打字；说“进入睡眠”暂停聆听，说“唤醒”继续。
它是为不方便用键盘鼠标的人设计的。它开着的时候，普通听写不可用，所以如果你只想用第 1 种方法，记得再把它关掉。

sections.heading: 3. 第三方语音输入应用
body: 如果你要说的是一段段话而不是一两句、经常中英混说，或者想保留说过的内容，就值得装一个第三方应用。可选的有[Superwhisper](superwhisper-alternative)、[VoiceInk](voiceink-alternative)、[Wispr Flow](wispr-flow-alternative)，以及我们做的 TypeAloud，[横向对比](best-dictation-apps-mac)里有它们的区别。
这些应用的设置大同小异：安装，授予麦克风权限和 macOS 辅助功能权限（有了它，应用才能往其他应用里输入文字），然后根据应用是本地还是云端，下载语音模型或登录账号。之后按下或按住应用的快捷键说话就行。

sections.heading: 该用哪个
body: 回消息、搜东西：系统听写。不用手操作 Mac：语音控制。用语音写文档、提示词、笔记：语音输入应用。系统听写出问题时，看 [Mac 听写不工作怎么办](mac-dictation-not-working)。

faq.q: Mac 听写的快捷键是什么？
faq.a: 在“系统设置 > 键盘 > 听写 > 快捷键”里自己选，键盘有麦克风键的话也可以直接按。第三方应用各有自己的快捷键。

faq.q: Mac 能用中文语音输入吗？
faq.a: 能。在“键盘 > 听写 > 语言”里加上普通话。系统听写一次只用一种语言；一句话里中英混说的情况，见[中英混合语音输入](chinese-english-dictation)。

faq.q: Mac 听写能离线用吗？
faq.a: “键盘”设置里会显示一般听写是否在设备上处理。其他离线方案见 [Mac 离线语音输入](offline-dictation-mac)。

faq.q: Mac 听写怎么关掉？
faq.a: 在“系统设置 > 键盘 > 听写”里关闭。如果开着语音控制，到“辅助功能”里关掉。

en.title: macOS Dictation not working or stopping? Fixes in order — TypeAloud
en.description: Apple's built-in Dictation won't start, stops on its own or mishears you? Check the shortcut, microphone source, Voice Control and language, based on Apple's documentation.
heading: macOS Dictation not working?
Check these, in this order.
en.intro: This guide is about Dictation, the voice typing built into macOS (System Settings > Keyboard > Dictation). Most problems with it come from four settings: Dictation itself, the microphone it listens to, Voice Control and the language. Work through them in order; the last section covers what to do if Dictation works but does not fit how you write.

sections.heading: It does not start
body: Check System Settings > Keyboard > Dictation is on, and note which shortcut is set; pressing a different key does nothing.
Check System Settings > Accessibility > Voice Control is off. While Voice Control is on, standard Dictation is unavailable.

sections.heading: It starts but hears nothing
body: In Keyboard > Dictation, set Microphone source to the microphone you are actually using. Automatic picks the device it thinks is most likely, which may be a monitor or headset you are not speaking into.
In System Settings > Sound > Input, select the same microphone and speak: the input level should move. If you use an external microphone, raise its input volume.

sections.heading: It stops on its own
body: Dictation has no length limit, but it ends after 30 seconds without speech. That is by design and cannot be changed. If you often stop for longer than that to think or read, see the last section.

sections.heading: It mishears you
body: Make sure the dictation language matches what you speak: add it under Keyboard > Dictation > Languages, and switch with the language indicator next to the cursor. Dictation works in one language at a time, so sentences that mix Chinese and English often go wrong. A model that detects language on the fly handles that better; see [mixed Chinese–English dictation](chinese-english-dictation).

sections.heading: Another option: a dictation app
body: For long writing, mixed languages or text you need to keep, a separate dictation app can do more than built-in Dictation: most let you decide when recording ends and keep a history. Options include [Superwhisper](superwhisper-alternative), [VoiceInk](voiceink-alternative), [Wispr Flow](wispr-flow-alternative) and TypeAloud, which we make; see the [roundup](best-dictation-apps-mac).

faq.q: Why does Mac dictation stop after a while?
faq.a: It ends automatically when no speech is detected for 30 seconds. There is no setting to change this.

faq.q: Why is the Dictation option missing or greyed out?
faq.a: Voice Control may be on, since it replaces Dictation, or the language and region may not support Dictation.

faq.q: Dictation works in some apps but not others. Why?
faq.a: Dictation types into the focused text field. Password fields and some secure inputs do not accept it.

faq.q: Is there a tool that does not stop on silence?
faq.a: Most third-party dictation apps start and stop with a shortcut rather than a silence timer. See [how to voice type on a Mac](how-to-voice-type-mac).

zh.title: Mac 自带听写不工作、自动停止？按这个顺序排查 — TypeAloud
zh.description: macOS 自带的听写打不开、自己停掉或者听不准？依据 Apple 官方说明，逐项检查快捷键、麦克风来源、语音控制和语言设置。
zh.eyebrow: 修复 macOS 自带听写
heading: Mac 自带的听写不工作？
按这个顺序检查。
zh.intro: 这篇讲的是 macOS 系统自带的听写功能（系统设置 > 键盘 > 听写）。它的问题大多出在四个设置：听写开关本身、它用的麦克风、语音控制，以及语言。按顺序一项项查；如果听写能用但不适合你的写作方式，最后一节讲别的选择。

sections.heading: 按了没反应
body: 确认“系统设置 > 键盘 > 听写”已打开，并看清设置的是哪个快捷键，按错了键不会有任何反应。
确认“系统设置 > 辅助功能 > 语音控制”是关着的。语音控制开着时，普通听写不可用。

sections.heading: 能启动，但听不到声音
body: 在“键盘 > 听写”里，把“麦克风来源”设成你实际在用的麦克风。“自动”会选它认为最可能的设备，可能是你没在用的显示器或耳机。
在“系统设置 > 声音 > 输入”里选同一个麦克风并说话，输入电平应该会跳动。用外接麦克风的话，把输入音量调高。

sections.heading: 说着说着自己停了
body: 听写没有总时长限制，但 30 秒没检测到语音就会结束。这是设计如此，没有设置可以改。如果你经常要停下来想很久或者看资料，见最后一节。

sections.heading: 识别不准
body: 确认听写语言和你说的语言一致：在“键盘 > 听写 > 语言”里添加，听写时用光标旁的语言标识切换。听写一次只用一种语言，所以中英混说的句子经常出错。能边说边判断语言的模型处理得更好，见[中英混合语音输入](chinese-english-dictation)。

sections.heading: 另一个选择：第三方语音输入应用
body: 写长内容、中英混说，或者需要保留说过的话，单独的语音输入应用能做的比系统听写多：多数可以由你决定什么时候结束录音，还会保留记录。可选的有[Superwhisper](superwhisper-alternative)、[VoiceInk](voiceink-alternative)、[Wispr Flow](wispr-flow-alternative)，以及我们做的 TypeAloud，见[横向对比](best-dictation-apps-mac)。

faq.q: Mac 听写为什么过一会儿就停？
faq.a: 30 秒没检测到语音时会自动结束，没有设置可以修改。

faq.q: 为什么听写选项不见了或是灰的？
faq.a: 可能是开着语音控制，它会替代听写；也可能是当前语言和地区不支持听写。

faq.q: 为什么有的应用能听写，有的不行？
faq.a: 听写输入到当前获得焦点的输入框。密码框和一些安全输入框不接受听写。

faq.q: 有没有不会因为静音自动停止的工具？
faq.a: 多数第三方听写应用用快捷键控制开始和结束，不靠静音计时。详见 [Mac 怎么语音输入](how-to-voice-type-mac)。

en.title: Private dictation on Mac: voice typing that never uploads your audio — TypeAloud
en.description: "Zero data retention" still means your voice goes to a server. How to tell local dictation from cloud dictation, how to check it yourself, and a free local option.
heading: Dictation that keeps
your voice on your Mac.
en.intro: Cloud dictation apps often promise zero data retention. That means your recording is deleted after it is processed, not that it never left your Mac. If you dictate client details, health information or unreleased work, the difference matters. Here is how to tell, and how to check.

sections.heading: Zero retention is not local
body: With a cloud app, every dictation is uploaded, transcribed on a server and usually passed through a language model for cleanup. A retention policy decides what happens afterwards. It cannot change the fact that the audio was sent, and you are trusting the provider and its subprocessors to follow it.

sections.heading: Three ways to check an app
body: After the model download, disconnect from every network and dictate. If it still works, transcription happens on your Mac. That proves it works offline; whether anything is uploaded after you reconnect is a question for the source code or a network monitor. Cloud apps such as [Wispr Flow](wispr-flow-alternative) and [Typeless](typeless-alternative) stop working.
Read the source if there is one. Handy, VoiceInk and TypeAloud, which we make, are [open source](open-source-dictation-mac): the code that records, transcribes and saves is public.
For macOS Dictation, System Settings > Keyboard shows whether general dictation is processed on your device.

sections.heading: What to check in any dictation app
body: Where speech is transcribed: on your Mac, or on a server. Whether an AI pass runs on the text, and where: some apps transcribe locally but send the text to a cloud model for cleanup. Whether the app keeps a history of what you said, where it is stored, for how long, and how to delete it. Whether you need an account, which ties your use to a profile.

As one example, TypeAloud, which we make, transcribes locally, keeps its History on the Mac and needs no account; it uses the network for the model download and updates, and uploads audio only if you add your own cloud API key.

faq.q: Does macOS Dictation upload my voice?
faq.a: For supported languages on recent Macs, general dictation can be processed on device; System Settings > Keyboard shows whether it is.

faq.q: Where are my transcripts stored?
faq.a: It depends on the app. Check whether it keeps a history, where, for how long and how to delete it. macOS Dictation keeps none.

faq.q: Is local dictation as accurate as cloud?
faq.a: There is no general answer; it depends on the model and the language. The difference you will notice is that cloud apps rewrite your words with AI on their servers, while local apps give a verbatim transcript unless they offer AI cleanup on the Mac.

faq.q: What does zero data retention mean?
faq.a: That the provider deletes your audio and text after processing. The audio is still uploaded first.

zh.title: 不上传录音的语音输入：Mac 上真正私密的听写 — TypeAloud
zh.description: “零数据留存”仍然意味着你的声音传到了服务器。怎么分辨本地听写和云端听写、怎么自己验证，以及一个免费的本地选择。
zh.nav: 不上传录音的语音输入
heading: 不上传录音的
Mac 语音输入。
zh.intro: 云端语音输入应用常常承诺“零数据留存”。这指的是录音处理完就删除，不是录音从没离开过你的 Mac。如果你口述的是客户资料、健康信息或未发布的工作，这个区别很要紧。下面讲怎么分辨，以及怎么验证。

sections.heading: 零留存不等于本地
body: 用云端应用时，每次听写都会上传，在服务器上转写，通常还要经过大模型整理。留存政策决定的是之后怎么处理，改变不了录音已经发出去的事实，你也只能相信服务商和它的下游供应商会照章执行。

sections.heading: 三种验证方法
body: 下载完模型后，断开所有网络再听写。还能用，说明转写在你的 Mac 上完成。这能证明它可以离线工作；重新联网后会不会上传，要看源代码或网络监控工具。[Wispr Flow](wispr-flow-alternative)、[Typeless](typeless-alternative) 这类云端应用会直接用不了。
有源代码就去看。Handy、VoiceInk 和我们做的 TypeAloud 都[开源](open-source-dictation-mac)，录音、转写、保存的代码都是公开的。
macOS 自带听写的话，“系统设置 > 键盘”里会显示一般听写是否在设备上处理。

sections.heading: 任何听写应用都该检查的几点
body: 语音在哪里转写：在你的 Mac 上，还是在服务器上。有没有 AI 处理文字、在哪里处理：有的应用本地转写，却把文字发到云端模型去整理。应用会不会保留说过的内容、存在哪里、保留多久、怎么删除。需不需要账号，账号会把你的使用记录和个人档案挂钩。
举个例子，我们做的 TypeAloud 在本地转写，历史记录存在 Mac 上，不需要账号；只有下载模型和更新会联网，填了你自己的云端 API key 才会上传音频。

faq.q: macOS 自带听写会上传我的声音吗？
faq.a: 在较新的 Mac 上，支持的语言可以在设备上处理一般听写；“系统设置 > 键盘”里会显示是否如此。

faq.q: 转写记录存在哪里？
faq.a: 取决于应用。看它是否保留记录、存在哪里、保留多久、怎么删除。macOS 自带听写不保留记录。

faq.q: 本地听写和云端一样准吗？
faq.a: 没有统一答案，取决于模型和语言。你能明显感到的区别是：云端应用会在服务器上用 AI 改写你的话，本地应用除非支持在本机做 AI 整理，否则给的是逐字转写。

faq.q: “零数据留存”是什么意思？
faq.a: 指服务商在处理完后删除你的音频和文字。音频仍然要先上传。

en.title: How to write long documents by voice on a Mac — TypeAloud
en.description: Dictate first drafts, reports and long emails on a Mac: how to structure what you say, record hands-free, avoid losing text, and edit afterwards.
heading: Write the first draft
by talking.
en.intro: Speaking is roughly three times faster than typing, and most of the time saved is in long text: drafts, reports, long emails, design docs. Dictating long text well is a skill of its own. These are the habits that make it work, whichever tool you use.

sections.heading: Talk from an outline
body: Type five or six headings first. Then dictate one section at a time, looking at the heading, as if explaining it to a colleague. Rambling comes from not knowing what comes next; an outline removes that.
Then work section by section: dictate one section, check the text has landed where you expect, and only then start the next. If something goes wrong, you lose a paragraph, not the draft.

sections.heading: Record hands-free for long passages
body: Holding a key for minutes is tiring. Most tools have a hands-free mode: macOS Dictation starts with one press and stops with another, and many apps offer a toggle (in TypeAloud, for example, a double-tap of the shortcut). Pause as long as you need to think, but with macOS Dictation keep it under 30 seconds or it ends the session.

sections.heading: Use a tool that keeps what you said
body: For long passages, a history matters: if something goes wrong at the end of five minutes, you want the text back. macOS Dictation does not keep one; most dictation apps do. Some also save the audio of a failed transcription so you can retry it.

sections.heading: Dictate now, edit later
body: Do not correct as you go. Get the whole draft out, then edit with the keyboard. If your tool rewrites speech with AI, decide whether you want that for a draft; a verbatim transcript keeps your own voice. Add names and terms to the tool's dictionary so they come out right the first time.

faq.q: Is there a limit on how long I can dictate?
faq.a: macOS Dictation has no length limit but ends after 30 seconds of silence. Cloud apps may cap words per week; local apps usually have no limit.

faq.q: What happens if transcription fails halfway?
faq.a: It depends on the tool. Apps with a history usually keep finished text; some also keep the audio so you can retry.

faq.q: Can I dictate in Chinese and English together?
faq.a: Yes. The local Qwen3-ASR model [detects the language as you speak](chinese-english-dictation).

faq.q: Should I speak punctuation?
faq.a: With macOS Dictation, auto-punctuation works in supported languages, and you can also say "comma" or "new paragraph". Many apps add punctuation automatically.

zh.title: 在 Mac 上用语音写长文：口述初稿的方法 — TypeAloud
zh.description: 在 Mac 上口述初稿、报告和长邮件：怎么组织要说的话、免按住录音、不丢内容，以及之后怎么修改。
heading: 初稿，
用说的写出来。
zh.intro: 说话大约比打字快三倍，省下的时间主要在长文本上：初稿、报告、长邮件、设计文档。把长内容说好本身是一门技巧。下面是让它行得通的几个习惯，用什么工具都适用。

sections.heading: 照着提纲说
body: 先打五六个小标题，然后看着标题一节一节地说，像在给同事讲解。说得啰嗦，往往是因为不知道下一句该说什么，有了提纲就不会。
然后一节一节来：说完一节，确认文字已经出现在你预期的位置，再开始下一节。万一出了问题，丢的是一段，而不是整篇初稿。

sections.heading: 长段内容用免提模式
body: 按着一个键说几分钟很累。多数工具都有免提模式：macOS 听写按一下开始、再按一下结束，很多应用也有切换模式（比如 TypeAloud 是双击快捷键）。中间停下来想多久都行，但用 macOS 听写时别超过 30 秒，否则它会结束这次听写。

sections.heading: 用一个会保存记录的工具
body: 说长段内容时，有没有记录很要紧：说了五分钟，最后出了问题，你会希望能把文字找回来。macOS 听写不保留记录，多数听写应用会保留，有的还会保存转写失败时的录音，方便重试。

sections.heading: 先说完，再修改
body: 别边说边改。先把整篇初稿说出来，再用键盘修改。如果你的工具会用 AI 改写，想想初稿要不要这样；逐字转写能保留你自己的口吻。把人名和术语加进工具的词典，第一遍就能写对。

faq.q: 一次能说多久？
faq.a: macOS 听写没有总时长限制，但 30 秒没声音就结束。云端应用可能有每周字数上限，本地应用通常不限。

faq.q: 转写到一半失败怎么办？
faq.a: 取决于工具。有历史记录的应用通常会保留已完成的文字，有的还会保留录音供重试。

faq.q: 能中英文一起说吗？
faq.a: 能。本地的 Qwen3-ASR 模型[边说边识别语言](chinese-english-dictation)。

faq.q: 标点要说出来吗？
faq.a: macOS 听写在支持的语言里会自动加标点，也可以说“逗号”“新段落”。很多应用会自动加标点。

en.title: How to voice type in Google Docs, Word, Notion, Obsidian, WeChat and more on Mac — TypeAloud
en.description: Which Mac apps have their own voice typing (Google Docs, Word, WeChat), which rely on system dictation (Notion, Obsidian, Slack), and how to get one shortcut that works everywhere.
heading: Voice typing in the apps
you already use.
en.intro: Some Mac apps have voice typing built in, some do not, and the ones that do all work differently. This guide goes app by app, then covers the two ways to get the same voice typing everywhere: macOS Dictation and system-wide dictation apps.

sections.heading: Google Docs
body: Docs has Voice typing under Tools > Voice typing, in current versions of Chrome, Edge and Safari. Allow microphone access, pick your language, then click the microphone to start and again to stop. In some languages you can say punctuation such as "comma" and "new paragraph"; editing commands work only in English. It only works inside Docs.

sections.heading: Microsoft Word
body: Word's Dictate button, on the Home tab, is available to Microsoft 365 subscribers, including on Mac. It processes audio in Microsoft's cloud, so it needs a connection.

sections.heading: WeChat
body: Since version 4.1.8, WeChat for Mac has voice input, and you can hold Fn to use it outside WeChat too. If you already have WeChat installed, that makes it a ready-made system-wide option; recognition runs in the cloud.

sections.heading: Notion, Obsidian and Slack
body: None of these has general voice typing of its own on Mac. Notion's AI meeting notes transcribe meetings, Obsidian has community plugins that send audio to a transcription service, and Slack offers audio clips rather than dictation. For typing by voice into them, use one of the system-wide options below.

sections.heading: One method for every app
body: macOS Dictation types into any focused text field, in any app, for free. Its limits are one language at a time, a stop after 30 seconds of silence and no history; see [how to set it up](how-to-voice-type-mac).

System-wide dictation apps do the same with their own shortcut and model, and usually add a history of what you said. They need macOS Accessibility permission, which is what lets an app type into other apps. Examples are [Wispr Flow](wispr-flow-alternative) (cloud), [Superwhisper](superwhisper-alternative) and TypeAloud, which we make (both local). The [roundup](best-dictation-apps-mac) compares more.

sections.heading: Secure fields and sending
body: Some secure fields, such as password boxes, block text inserted by other apps. Most dictation tools only insert text and leave sending to you, but some can press Enter on a spoken keyword or send automatically; check that setting before dictating into chat.

faq.q: How do I voice type in Google Docs on a Mac?
faq.a: Open the document in Chrome, Edge or Safari, choose Tools > Voice typing, then click the microphone.

faq.q: Does Word for Mac have dictation?
faq.a: Yes, the Dictate button on the Home tab, for Microsoft 365 subscribers. It needs an internet connection.

faq.q: Can I dictate into Notion or Obsidian?
faq.a: Yes, with macOS Dictation or a system-wide dictation app; neither app has its own general voice typing.

faq.q: Why does a dictation app need Accessibility permission?
faq.a: macOS requires it before an app can type text into other apps or listen for a global shortcut.

zh.title: 在 Google Docs、Word、Notion、Obsidian、微信里怎么语音输入（Mac） — TypeAloud
zh.description: Mac 上哪些应用自带语音输入（Google Docs、Word、微信），哪些要靠系统听写（Notion、Obsidian、Slack），以及怎么用一个快捷键在所有应用里语音输入。
heading: 在你常用的应用里
怎么语音输入。
zh.intro: Mac 上的应用，有的自带语音输入，有的没有，自带的做法也各不相同。这篇逐个应用说明，最后讲两种在所有应用里都能用的办法：macOS 自带听写和系统级听写应用。

sections.heading: Google Docs
body: Docs 在“工具 > 语音输入”里有语音输入，支持最新版的 Chrome、Edge 和 Safari。允许麦克风访问、选好语言，点麦克风开始，再点一次停止。部分语言可以口述标点，比如“逗号”“新段落”；编辑类语音命令只支持英文。它只在 Docs 里有效。

sections.heading: Microsoft Word
body: Word“开始”选项卡上的“听写”按钮，Microsoft 365 订阅用户可以用，Mac 版也有。音频在微软的云端处理，所以要联网。

sections.heading: 微信
body: 从 4.1.8 起，Mac 微信支持语音输入，在微信外也可以按住 Fn 使用。如果你已经装了微信，这就是一个现成的系统级方案，识别在云端完成。

sections.heading: Notion、Obsidian 和 Slack
body: 这几个在 Mac 上都没有通用的语音输入。Notion 的 AI 会议记录用来转写会议，Obsidian 有把音频发到转写服务的社区插件，Slack 提供的是语音片段而不是听写。要在它们里面用语音打字，用下面两种系统级的办法。

sections.heading: 一个办法通吃所有应用
body: macOS 自带听写能输入到任何应用里获得焦点的输入框，而且免费。限制是一次一种语言、30 秒没声音就停、不保留记录，设置方法见 [Mac 怎么语音输入](how-to-voice-type-mac)。

系统级听写应用用自己的快捷键和模型做同样的事，通常还会保存说过的内容。它们需要 macOS 的辅助功能权限，有了这个权限，应用才能往其他应用里输入文字。例子有 [Wispr Flow](wispr-flow-alternative)（云端）、[Superwhisper](superwhisper-alternative) 和我们做的 TypeAloud（都是本地）。更多对比见[横向对比](best-dictation-apps-mac)。

sections.heading: 安全输入框和发送
body: 一些安全输入框，比如密码框，会拦截其他应用插入的文字。多数听写工具只负责输入、由你自己发送，但也有工具能用口令按回车或自动发送，往聊天框里听写之前看一下这个设置。

faq.q: Mac 上 Google Docs 怎么语音输入？
faq.a: 在 Chrome、Edge 或 Safari 里打开文档，选“工具 > 语音输入”，点麦克风。

faq.q: Mac 版 Word 有听写吗？
faq.a: 有，“开始”选项卡上的“听写”按钮，需要 Microsoft 365 订阅，并且要联网。

faq.q: Notion 和 Obsidian 里能语音输入吗？
faq.a: 能，用 macOS 自带听写或系统级听写应用。这两个应用本身没有通用的语音输入。

faq.q: 听写应用为什么要辅助功能权限？
faq.a: macOS 规定，应用要往其他应用里输入文字或监听全局快捷键，必须先获得这个权限。

en.title: Speech to text on Mac: live dictation vs transcribing recordings — TypeAloud
en.description: Two different jobs share the name speech to text: typing by voice as you go, and transcribing audio files. Which Mac tools do which, and what is free.
heading: Speech to text on a Mac:
two different jobs.
en.intro: "Speech to text" covers two jobs. One is dictation: turning what you say into text in the app you are using. The other is transcription: you have a recording and want a transcript. Tools are usually good at one of them. Picking the right kind saves most of the frustration.

table.caption: Speech to text tools on Mac by job
rows: Yes, into any app; free, local
Yes, in the version sold on its website (not the App Store one)

sections.heading: Dictation into apps
body: For writing by voice, you want something that works in every app and puts text at the cursor. macOS Dictation does this for short text; see [how to voice type on a Mac](how-to-voice-type-mac). Third-party apps such as [Superwhisper](superwhisper-alternative), [VoiceInk](voiceink-alternative), [Wispr Flow](wispr-flow-alternative) and TypeAloud, which we make add a history, AI cleanup or local models.

sections.heading: Transcribing recordings
body: For interviews, lectures and meetings you want batch import, speaker labels and export to subtitles or documents. MacWhisper is the specialist here; see [Superwhisper vs MacWhisper](superwhisper-vs-macwhisper) for how it compares.

sections.heading: Offline either way
body: Both jobs can run on an Apple Silicon Mac without uploading audio. If privacy matters, choose local models; see [offline dictation for Mac](offline-dictation-mac).

faq.q: What is the best free speech to text on Mac?
faq.a: For dictation, macOS Dictation is built in; Superwhisper's free tier, Spokenly and TypeAloud are free apps. For files, MacWhisper's free version handles basic transcription.

faq.q: Can dictation apps transcribe audio files?
faq.a: Some can: Superwhisper on Pro, MacWhisper by design. Others, including macOS Dictation and TypeAloud, only take live speech.

faq.q: Does speech to text on Mac work in Chinese?
faq.a: Yes. macOS Dictation supports Mandarin as a dictation language, and Chinese-trained models such as Qwen3-ASR handle mixed Chinese–English.

faq.q: Does speech to text on Mac need internet?
faq.a: Not necessarily. macOS Dictation can process on device for supported languages, and local apps run offline. See [offline dictation on Mac](offline-dictation-mac).

zh.title: Mac 语音转文字：实时听写和录音转写，分清再选 — TypeAloud
zh.description: “语音转文字”其实是两件事：边说边打字，以及把录音文件转成文字。Mac 上哪些工具做哪件事，哪些免费。
heading: Mac 上的语音转文字，
其实是两件事。
zh.intro: “语音转文字”包含两件事。一是口述输入：把你说的话变成当前应用里的文字。二是录音转写：你有一段录音，想要文字稿。工具通常只擅长其中一件，选对类型就能省掉大部分麻烦。
